messages.subject: Wallace v1.0.6.3 on CRAN
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

There is a new version available on CRAN <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/wallace/index.html>. This new version now can turn on/off clamp for the maxent.jar option thanks to the newest Maxent java version (v3.4.4 <https://biodiversityinformatics.amnh.org/open_source/maxent/>). The previous Wallace version just had this option available for the maxnet package (Maxent implementation on R).

Best,
Gonzalo

messages.subject: Uncertainty associated to model output
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

As far as I know, Wallace does not have the option to replicate the final model, so uncertainty regarding that model is unknown. Taking into consideration its importance, specially when trying to publish one's results, I would like to ask wether there is a way to obtain the uncertainty associated to model outputs and predictions? Maybe using other packages for post-processing the Wallace output?

I used Wallace to perform ecological niche modelling, and the lack of uncertainty information was one of the crucial negative points highlighted by the reviewers.

Thank you very much,

Sebastià

messages.subject: Re: Uncertainty associated to model output
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sebastià,

You are right that you cannot run replicates within Wallace although the statistics you get from the ENMeval are the result of the partitioning scheme you used and thus you get information on the mean and sd of your test statistics. If you want to run replicates you can use the RMD file to run your models in R and replicate those.

Best,

Andrea
